Through these observations, I discovered that love at UCSB takes many forms and is often expressed through ordinary interactions. Whether it appears in a quiet embrace between romantic partners, a student-led act of kindness, or a group of friends spending time together, love contributes to a sense of connection and belonging on campus.

The Unit 2 readings helped me understand that love is not only a feeling but also a practice of care, vulnerability, and support. My observations confirmed these ideas by showing how students build meaningful relationships through everyday actions. At the same time, they revealed that love can exist on a broader community level, helping people feel included and emotionally supported even outside close personal relationships.

Overall, this field experience demonstrated that love is woven into daily campus life. Although these moments may seem small, they play an important role in creating a welcoming environment where students can develop relationships, find support, and experience a sense of belonging.
